analysis.title: GWIS: datacentres - catalysts, context and next week's big summit in Texas
key_insights: Graham Ambrose (GS FICC and Equities, not Global Investment Research) says the debate over US datacenter construction after the US mid-terms is one of the most pivotal issues for APAC equities. The aggregate GIR view is that the market is too concerned: there will be some delays, but this will extend the cycle.

Datacenter projects already under construction support strong spending growth through 2027 (86 GW) and underpin just above half of GIR's 2028 spending forecasts. Visibility is more limited beyond 2028, and the 2029-2030 outlook depends on announced projects converting to construction.
States where Democrats are likely to further restrict data center development account for roughly 45% of planned US data center capacity. Texas alone accounts for roughly 25%.
GIR sees a potential restriction outcome as smoothing spending and extending the duration of the cycle, rather than reducing the total addressable market (TAM).

Current project timelines imply ~55 GW of capacity energizing in 2028, out of 86 GW under construction now. High probability announcements add 171 GW and medium/low probability announcements add 293 GW.

GIR datacenter construction capex forecasts, at a baseline of ~$3.5bn construction spending per GW (Census Bureau construction scope, excluding servers, racks, GPUs and network equipment): $80bn in 2026, $100bn in 2027, $125bn in 2028. Hyperscaler capex is $829bn in 2026, an estimated $1.2 trillion in 2027 and $1.4 trillion in 2028.

Gina Hinojosa (D) won the Texas governor race against Greg Abbott (R). She has suggested a moratorium on data centers until the legislature adds protections in 2027, including proof that facilities will not raise residential electricity or water rates, and dedicated incremental generation for mega-scale sites.

US Senate (12 Nov-20 Dec) will consider the Ratepayer Protection Act and transmission permitting reform. Lame-duck passage starts a 12-month statutory clock for utilities to implement dedicated high-load tariffs, shifting grid upgrade capex onto hyperscalers.

New York Senate decision deadline on 31 December on the Responsible Data Center Development Act would codify Executive Order 62 into a permanent statewide moratorium, with proposed thresholds as low as 20 MW, freezing greenfield pipelines in the state.

ERCOT / Texas PUC is due to finalize its Large Flexible Load Grid Reliability Audit in Q1/27. It governs the stalled 'Batch Zero' interconnection queue and sets energization timelines, curtailment protocols and backup generation obligations for data centers above 75 MW under Texas Senate Bill 6.

The TomorrowX AI summit in Austin, Texas (17-18 November) has a line-up including Jensen Huang, Michael Dell, Lisa Su, Stan Druckenmiller, Marc Rowan, Dina Powell McCormick, David Sacks, Brannin McBee, Scott DeBoer and Rene Haas. GS is gathering investors for an event there.

sector_views.rationale: GIR view is that the market is too concerned about restrictions. Delays would extend the cycle rather than cut the TAM.

risk_factors: State-level moratoria or restrictions in states holding roughly 45% of planned US data center capacity, with Texas at roughly 25%.
New York's Responsible Data Center Development Act could codify a permanent moratorium with thresholds as low as 20 MW.
The lame-duck Ratepayer Protection Act could shift grid upgrade costs onto hyperscalers.
ERCOT's Large Flexible Load audit could impose curtailment and backup generation obligations on data centers above 75 MW.
Visibility on 2029-2030 spending depends on announced projects converting to construction.
geopolitical: US post-midterm politics: Democratic gains and the Texas governor result raise the chance of state-level data center restrictions.
Federal legislation: Ratepayer Protection Act and transmission permitting reform under consideration in the US Senate lame-duck session.

tension_points.bull_case: GIR sees restrictions as causing some delays that smooth spending and extend the cycle's duration, with 86 GW already under construction supporting growth through 2027 and just above half of 2028 forecasts.
tension_points.bear_case: Democratic-leaning states hold roughly 45% of planned US capacity (Texas ~25%), and moratoria, ratepayer rules and interconnection delays could slow conversion of announced projects, limiting 2029-2030 visibility.
tension_points.what_invalidates: New York Senate enactment of the Responsible Data Center Development Act by 31 December, or lame-duck passage of the Ratepayer Protection Act, would test the view.

theme_stances.key_argument: The market is too concerned about datacenter restrictions, which will delay but extend the cycle rather than reduce the TAM.
theme_stances.evidence: The aggregate GIR view is that the market is too concerned.
